title: The budget disappears a week before
situation: You and five other students are running a free weekend coding workshop for sixty school pupils at a community centre. A week before, the student council cuts your grant in half. The money for the room and the lunches is gone, and the room deposit is due on Friday.
goal: Decide with the team what happens to the workshop. There is no single right way to do it.

character.name: Aigerim
character.wants: To cancel before the team owes money it cannot pay

hiddenMotive: She approved the budget without a backup plan and is afraid the team will blame her for the gap.

beats.goal: Aigerim breaks the news and says the workshop should be cancelled.

answerTypes.description: slows things down and asks what exactly changed
examples: Okay, let's slow down. What exactly did the council change?
Thanks for telling me straight away. Walk me through the numbers.
Before we decide anything, tell me what we still have.
answerTypes.characterIntent: explains the numbers and relaxes a little, relieved to share it.

answerTypes.description: agrees to cancel at once
examples: Then we cancel, there's no other way.
Let's just call it off and tell everyone.
If the money is gone, the workshop is gone.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is surprised the leader gives up so fast, and asks whether there really is nothing else.

answerTypes.description: looks for whose fault it is
examples: How did we not see this coming?
Who signed the budget without a backup?
Somebody should have checked this earlier.
answerTypes.characterIntent: gets defensive and says she did the budget the way everyone agreed.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: repeats that the deposit is due on Friday and asks what the leader wants to do.

beats.goal: With half the money, what can the team still do?

answerTypes.description: proposes new ways to cover the gap and names the risk
examples: We could ask the university for a free room, but it might not be ready in time.
Let's ask local cafés to sponsor lunch. The risk is they say no by Friday.
What if pupils bring their own laptops? Some won't have one, so we'd need a backup.
answerTypes.characterIntent: likes that there is a plan B and asks what matters most if it only half works.

answerTypes.description: keeps the workshop but makes it smaller
examples: We run it for thirty pupils instead of sixty.
Let's make it one day instead of two.
We keep the workshop and drop the lunches.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees it fits the budget and asks what they are really trying to keep.

answerTypes.description: has nothing to offer and hands the problem back
examples: I don't know, you're the treasurer.
I have no idea what we can do.
Maybe it will sort itself out.
answerTypes.characterIntent: goes quiet, then says the team chat is falling apart.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: asks which part of the workshop the leader would protect first.

beats.goal: The team chat is in panic, and two members say they want to quit.

answerTypes.description: calms the team and gets them working together
examples: Let's get everyone on a call tonight and look at it together.
Tell them we're not cancelling yet, we still have a week.
Panic won't help. Let's split what each of us checks today.
answerTypes.characterIntent: sounds calmer and says she'll post that they are meeting tonight.

answerTypes.description: lets people leave without trying to keep them
examples: If they want to quit, let them.
We'll manage without them.
I can't stop people from leaving.
answerTypes.characterIntent: is uneasy and says that leaves four people to do everything.

answerTypes.description: wants to keep the problem from the team
examples: Don't tell the others yet.
Let's keep this between us for now.
No need to worry the team.
answerTypes.characterIntent: points out that the others already know.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: asks what she should tell the team.

beats.goal: What matters most for the pupils?

answerTypes.description: protects what the pupils came for
examples: What matters is that the pupils actually build something.
The teaching is the point; the lunches are a nice extra.
Let's keep what helps the kids learn and cut the rest.
answerTypes.characterIntent: agrees, then says they only have seats for thirty of the sixty who signed up.

answerTypes.description: refuses to cut anything
examples: We promised everything, so we keep everything.
Cutting anything would look bad.
We'll find the money somehow for all of it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: reminds the leader that the numbers do not allow it, and brings up the seats.

answerTypes.description: wants the team or the teachers to decide
examples: Let's ask the team what they think matters most.
Can we get everyone to vote on what to keep?
What do the pupils' teachers care about most?
answerTypes.characterIntent: says it's a good idea but they still need to decide who gets the seats.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: moves on to the seats: sixty signed up, thirty fit.

beats.goal: Sixty pupils signed up and there are seats for thirty. Who gets in?

answerTypes.description: picks a rule everyone can see and explains it
examples: First come, first served, and we tell everyone why.
We draw lots in public so nobody feels cheated.
We keep half the seats for pupils who've never coded.
answerTypes.characterIntent: says that is fair and asks what has to happen before Friday.

answerTypes.description: picks people the team knows or likes
examples: Let's keep the places for our friends' younger siblings.
Take the pupils who already know some code, they'll learn fastest.
Pick the ones we already know.
answerTypes.characterIntent: hesitates and says the other families will notice.

answerTypes.description: does not want to tell the others they are out
examples: Let's not tell the others they're out until the last day.
Just stop replying to the extra ones.
They'll figure it out.
answerTypes.characterIntent: worries that thirty families will turn up on the day.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: says the seats can wait and asks about Friday's deposit.

beats.goal: The deposit is due Friday. What happens by then, and who does it?

answerTypes.description: gives each task an owner and a deadline
examples: You call the council by Wednesday, I book the free room today, Madi asks the cafés.
By Friday: new room confirmed, sponsors asked, seats announced. Each of us owns one.
Here's the plan: three tasks, three owners, and we check in on Thursday evening.
answerTypes.characterIntent: takes her task, then comes back on Thursday with bad news.

answerTypes.description: hopes it works out
examples: Let's all try our best this week.
We'll see how it goes.
Everyone help where they can.
answerTypes.characterIntent: asks what she personally should do, and gets no answer, then the bad news arrives.

answerTypes.description: takes every task
examples: I'll handle all of it myself.
Leave it to me, I'll sort everything.
It's faster if I just do it.
answerTypes.characterIntent: offers to help and is turned down, then the bad news arrives.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: says she'll do what she can, then comes back on Thursday with bad news.

beats.goal: Thursday: the free room fell through. Only a small room for twenty is left.

answerTypes.description: adapts the plan and brings the team along
examples: Okay, we run two sessions of ten in the smaller room.
Let's regroup and see what we can still offer.
It's a blow, but we can split the day into shifts.
answerTypes.characterIntent: laughs with relief and says she'll tell the team.

answerTypes.description: stops trying
examples: That's it, we cancel.
I told you this wouldn't work.
There's no point anymore.
answerTypes.characterIntent: quietly agrees and says she'll write to the families.

answerTypes.description: promises to fix it single-handed
examples: I'll find another room tonight, whatever it takes.
We'll squeeze all thirty in somehow.
I'll stay up and fix it myself.
answerTypes.characterIntent: warns that nobody can find a room for thirty overnight.

examples: ok
hmm
fallback.characterIntent: says they need to decide by tonight, and the scene ends.
